name: Premium Residency -- Real Estate Owner Residency

requirements.blocker_text: Requires ownership of Saudi real estate worth at least SAR 4 million (approx. USD 1.07 million), in a location and property class approved under the January 2026 foreign property ownership law -- eligible in most major cities (Riyadh, Jeddah, NEOM, Qiddiya, Red Sea Global) but explicitly excluding Makkah and Madinah.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase or already own qualifying Saudi property worth at least SAR 4 million in an eligible city outside Makkah and Madinah.

evidence_required.document: Title deed or verified property-ownership documentation meeting the SAR 4 million threshold
Medical examination and criminal-background check from country of origin

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum physical presence requirement to maintain the residency

sources.title: Premium Residency Center (pr.gov.sa) -- official Saudi government portal, Real Estate Owner Residency product. Direct automated fetch is blocked by robots.txt; figures cross-verified against secondary sources and my.gov.sa's official listing (see sa_premium_residency_investor_entrepreneur for the same sourcing-method caveat, which applies identically here)

Mirabello Consultancy -- Saudi Premium Residency 2026 guide, describing the January 2026 foreign property ownership law and the SAR 4 million Real Estate Owner threshold in detail, including the Makkah/Madinah exclusion
GCC Relocation Hub -- Saudi Premium Residency 2026 full eligibility guide, independent cross-check of the SAR 4 million property threshold

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING, one of the sharpest single-year regulatory shifts found anywhere in this dataset: this entire route was effectively non-viable before January 2026, when a new foreign property ownership law opened Saudi real estate to foreign buyers across most major cities for the first time -- before that, foreign real estate ownership in Saudi Arabia was tightly restricted, making the Real Estate Owner Premium Residency product largely theoretical. The Makkah/Madinah exclusion is notable and not incidental: it reflects the two holy cities' distinct legal and religious-significance status rather than an ordinary zoning restriction, and is worth surfacing prominently on any route detail page rather than treating as a routine geographic carve-out. Same sourcing-method limitation as sa_premium_residency_investor_entrepreneur applies here: pr.gov.sa blocks automated fetching, so the SAR 4 million figure rests on strong convergent secondary-source corroboration (3+ independent sources, all dated 2026, all agreeing) rather than a directly fetched primary page -- flagged honestly as a follow-up target rather than treated as fully tier-1 verified in the strictest sense. The Makkah/Madinah exclusion is folded into re_property_value's blocker_text rather than modeled as its own requirement: the schema's closed attribute list has no clean fit for 'property location' (current_location represents the applicant's own location, not an asset's), and forcing that mismatch would repeat the same imperfect-attribute-fit issue flagged on Poland's repatriation route -- honest simplification over a technically-wrong formal requirement.
